deep.reconstruction:
Context: a mechanical variational principle for a system with generalized coordinates x_ι (ι = 1..n) and velocities x'_ι = dx_ι/dt. The aim of the page is to derive the Lagrange equations and then check the energy (vis viva) identity when V is a quadratic form in the velocities.

(1) Riemann writes δ∫(U + T + V) dt = 0. He starts to vary term by term: ∫(δU + ∂T/∂x δx ...). This line is struck out.

(2) He varies the velocity-dependent part V(x, x'). Integrating by parts in t (boundary terms dropped, my addition), the coefficient of δx_ι in the integrand is ∂V/∂x_ι − d/dt(∂V/∂x'_ι).

(3) Collecting the contribution of the position-dependent terms into a generalized force X_ι (e.g. X_ι = ∂(U+T)/∂x_ι; this reading is mine), the equations of motion are
X_ι + ∂V/∂x_ι − d/dt(∂V/∂x'_ι) = 0.
These are Lagrange's equations of the second kind.

(4) He specializes to V = Σ_{ι,ι'} a_{ι,ι'}(x) x'_ι x'_{ι'}, with a symmetric and summed over all ordered pairs, so there is no factor 1/2. Then
- ∂V/∂x_{ι''} = Σ ∂a_{ι,ι'}/∂x_{ι''} x'_ι x'_{ι'}
- ∂V/∂x'_{ι''} = 2 Σ_ι a_{ι,ι''} x'_ι.
He multiplies the Lagrange expression by x'_{ι''} and sums over ι'':
Σ_{ι''} ( Σ ∂a_{ι,ι'}/∂x_{ι''} x'_ι x'_{ι'} − d/dt[2 Σ a_{ι,ι''} x'_ι] ) x'_{ι''}.

(5) Evaluating this:
- The first term gives Σ (da_{ι,ι'}/dt) x'_ι x'_{ι'}, by the chain rule da/dt = Σ ∂a/∂x_{ι''} x'_{ι''}.
- The second term gives −2 Σ (da_{ι,ι''}/dt) x'_ι x'_{ι''} − 2 Σ a_{ι,ι''} x''_ι x'_{ι''}.
This matches his last line. The small '−2' mark over the first sum appears to note that combining the first two sums gives net coefficient −1.

(6) Implicit conclusion (mine): the total is −Σ (da/dt) x'x' − 2 Σ a x'' x' = −dV/dt. Hence Σ X_ι x'_ι = dV/dt, and if X_ι = −∂Π/∂x_ι this gives d(V + Π)/dt = 0, i.e. conservation of energy.

This is a routine scratch derivation of the energy integral from the Lagrange equations for a quadratic kinetic energy. The previous page (Green/Stokes-type line integral over an annulus) and the next page (algebra) are unrelated.
errors: No mathematical errors. The step of multiplying by x'_{ι''}, summing, and using the chain rule is correct, and ∂V/∂x'_{ι''} = 2Σ a_{ι,ι''} x'_ι correctly uses the symmetry of a.
The final simplification to −dV/dt is not written out; it is left implicit.
The roles of U and T are not specified on the page. The struck-out line suggests an abandoned first attempt at the variation.

results.what: Euler–Lagrange equations X_ι + ∂V/∂x_ι − d/dt ∂V/∂x'_ι = 0 from δ∫(U+T+V)dt = 0
results.modern_name: Lagrange's equations of the second kind / Hamilton's principle

results.what: For V = Σ a_{ιι'}(x) x'_ι x'_{ι'}, Σ_k x'_k (∂V/∂x_k − d/dt ∂V/∂x'_k) = −dV/dt, giving the energy integral
results.modern_name: Energy conservation for a quadratic kinetic energy (Euler's homogeneous function theorem applied to the Lagrangian / Jacobi energy integral)

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook analytical mechanics (Lagrange's equations and the energy integral for a quadratic kinetic energy) that was standard well before 1853; it is a scratch computation with nothing novel.

Equals 0: ∂V/∂x'_1 = 2 Σ_ι a_{ι,1} x'_ι, Riemann's term inside d/dt.
Equals 0: Σ_k x'_k ∂V/∂x_k = Σ (da_{ιι'}/dt) x'_ι x'_{ι'} by the chain rule, as in Riemann's first term.

Above the first sum on the last line there is a small overlined mark '−2' (or '2') written over x'_ι x'_{ι'}. It is not in the transcription and appears to record that the first two sums combine to coefficient −1.
